en.title: Codebase Memory MCP: Local Code Knowledge Graph for AI Agents
en.summary: Codebase Memory MCP is a locally run MCP server that indexes code, documentation, configuration, and infrastructure into a persistent graph for coding agents and CLI queries.
en.detail: Codebase Memory MCP is the DeusData repository and product: a locally run MCP server that builds a persistent knowledge graph from a project’s source code and surrounding technical context. It can help an agent trace symbols and dependencies or explore an unfamiliar repository, and it also offers a CLI. The project is separate from Graphify: shared graph terminology does not make them one product. Its optional CBM Lens is a companion interface within this project, not a separate Tool. The repository currently identifies MIT licensing and a release stream; its latest listed release at review was v0.12.1. Local indexing and graph queries do not require a hosted service or API key, according to the project. Installation, native build prerequisites, supported clients, performance and the optional Lens/model behavior are implementation- and version-dependent; review the current repository before use.
bestFor: Developers who want a local code graph exposed to MCP-compatible coding agents
Teams exploring relationships across source, docs, configuration, and infrastructure
Users who prefer local indexing and CLI or agent workflows
notIdealFor: People seeking a hosted no-setup SaaS
Users who need independently verified enterprise support or service-level commitments
Projects whose environment cannot meet the current native build or client-integration requirements
limitations: The core product is software that users install and operate; this is not a hosted code-analysis service.
The repository's performance and compatibility statements are vendor-maintained and were not independently benchmarked here.
Native build prerequisites and supported integrations can vary by platform and release.
CBM Lens is described by the project as an open-beta companion; its optional browser AI is opt-in and local according to the repository.
No account-level, team-hosting, security-audit, or commercial support claim is made by this review.
en.pricingSummary: The repository is MIT-licensed and the software is presented as locally runnable without a hosted API key. Compute and maintenance are the user's responsibility; any third-party model or infrastructure costs are separate and not established as a standard plan.

en.title: DeepSeek Harness: Open-Source Agent Workspace in Public Preview
en.summary: DeepSeek Harness is an open-source agent harness with a desktop app or code-launched web UI and a plugin-based architecture; it remains in public preview with rapidly changing compatibility.
en.detail: DeepSeek Harness is DeepSeek's user-facing open-source agent workspace and extensible harness, presented for everyday work, coding, research, background tasks, and plugin development. The official product page says it is in public preview worldwide. DeepSeek's GitHub repository labels it developer-preview software and warns that compatibility-breaking changes will occur. It can run as a desktop app or a web UI launched from code; using the web UI requires choosing a workspace and configuring a model/provider. The official privacy policy distinguishes official-model services from custom-model services: custom-model inputs are routed to the selected provider under that provider's policies, while the policy also lists session logs and user-provided content among data processed in connection with the services. The exact mode-specific capture and retention behavior was not independently tested, so do not generalize a privacy guarantee. The official safety notice says the software has not undergone a security audit and can execute generated code, commands, plugins, and access available files, processes, network, or credentials. Use least privilege and an isolated disposable environment; do not treat it as production-ready. No fixed all-in price or account-level usage allowance is asserted.

Users comfortable configuring model providers and reviewing tool permissions
Experimentation in a disposable or isolated development environment
notIdealFor: Production or sensitive-data workloads without an independent security review
Users seeking a stable compatibility contract or fully managed no-setup service
Users expecting model inference, API access, or plugins to be free of separate provider charges
limitations: Public preview / developer preview; interfaces and compatibility may change rapidly and break.
The official repository says it has not undergone a security audit; generated code/commands and plugins may access files, processes, network, and credentials available to the process.
Sandboxing and approval prompts reduce but do not eliminate risk; the official guidance recommends least privilege and a disposable VM/container.
Model setup and costs depend on the chosen official or custom provider; no single all-in price or quota was verified.

This product is distinct from DeepSeek model versions; bundled model names and versions must be maintained as version claims, not separate Tool IDs.
en.pricingSummary: Open-source software is offered in public preview, but this does not establish zero total cost. Model/API charges depend on the selected provider and configuration; no universal subscription price or quota was verified.
